name: Cameroon
headline: Cameroon: +3.5% growth in 2025, 3.5% inflation, debt 41% of GDP
sections: Cameroon is a $59.2 billion economy (2025), the world's 94th-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +3.5% in 2025, close to the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $5,788 at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 14.6% of GDP (2025).
Consumer prices rose 3.5% in 2025, broadly within typical target ranges, down from 6.3% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 3.6% (2025), below the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 6.5% (2025).
Gross government debt is 41% of GDP (2025), a moderate level that has fallen from 45% in 2020. The general government balance is −2.1% of GDP (2025).
The current account balance is −3.8% of GDP (2025). Trade equals 33% of GDP (2025), a relatively closed economy. Net FDI inflows were 1.0% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 34% of GDP by 2031, on a declining path from today's level. Life expectancy is 64.0 years (2024). Population: 29.9 million (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
